prompt: Review the current Pocket Spatial browser DSP and propose concrete changes so the sliders produce profound, unmistakable perceptual changes, with the top 20-30% intentionally capable of sounding excessive or unnatural. The design goal is the strongest convincing 3D illusion possible from stereo playback through two physical speakers/home-theater front channels, not merely wider stereo. Inspect the current implementation in apps/pocket-spatial.html and apps/pocket-spatial-core.js. Focus especially on making Angle, Spatial Amount, Depth, Room Wrap, and related controls perceptually much stronger.
context: Pocket Spatial streams Audius live into an HTMLAudioElement, then processes it in Web Audio before output.

Current controls include Spatial Amount, Virtual Speaker Angle, Interaural Delay Stretch, Head-Shadow Cutoff, Cross-Ear Polarity, Early Reflection Depth, Room Time Scale, Room Wrap/Immersion, and Reflection Tone.

Several controls already use exponential mappings and the graph includes direct, cross-ear delayed/filtered paths, early reflections, later cross-fed room-wrap arrivals, automatic master trim, and a limiter.
The user reports that Angle still feels weak and that the overall result still does not feel profoundly present in the room or deeply immersive.
The listening target is stereo speakers/home theater, so transaural/crosstalk-cancellation ideas are welcome if they can be implemented in Web Audio without requiring measured HRTFs.
Keep output safety: extreme settings should become spatially bizarre or excessive, not merely much louder.
expected_response: Give a prioritized engineering review with specific Web Audio node-topology changes, formulas or mappings, concrete delay/gain/filter ranges, recommended defaults and extreme values, and any transaural/crosstalk-cancellation strategy that could materially deepen the 3D illusion. Identify why the current sliders feel weak and propose the smallest high-impact changes first. Include implementation cautions for physical speakers and iPhone/Web Audio.
